newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: LWR to do more business offshore - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: LWR to do more business offshore - NZPA.

text.p: Leading apparel manufacturer LWR Industries said on Thursday it would respond to speedier tariff reductions in last week's budget by shifting production offshore and importing more.

The New Zealand Press Association reported the Christchurch-based firm, which employs 1000 people in New Zealand, would not comment on the prospect for employees or the impact of the tariff policy on its profits.
General manager of corporate services Glenn Keen said the tariff policy, which seeks to remove tariffs on imports by 2010, would impact on the company.
"It'll impact but we'll just adopt different strategies. There'll be less manufacturing onshore and we will do more importing," he said.
"We'll have to move more of our manufacturing offshore and supply export markets from there."
Likely places were Australia or South Africa "which were not penalised so much". LWR currently manufacturers in both counties.
However, there were no immediate plans and markets would be monitored over time.
LWR earlier this year instituted a search for an international partner but called it off after failing to find anyone suitable. Nothing had changed with this issue, Keen said.
He said the company currently sells 43 percent of total turnover to overseas customers but he refused to disclose how much is currently manufactured offshore.
Commenting on the tariff, Keen said LWR was also able to import successfully as it was a large manufacturer in New Zealand.
"If you are importing, and obviously that is the cheapest way of doing things, you need long lead times.
"And you need large ranges. If you can't support that then you really can't order out of China."
"Because we are a large manufacturer we can do that for some of our lines. But we will have to move more."
LWR currently imports about 12 percent of its total New Zealand sales.
